newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST -Severn Trent eyed for value return.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Severn Trent eyed for value return.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Plc should see higher year profits and dividend when it reports on June 10 and will be eyed for any update on returning value to shareholders, analysts said.
"They have said there is more to come on buybacks, so we will be watching for an update," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Severn Trent said in March that it proposed to complete a plan to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares, announced in November, after picking up some 4.9 percent on the market and a small stake from the government in December.
It made the move after its planned bid for colleague South West Water was blocked by the previous Conservative government last year, along with a rival offer from Wessex Water .
Pretax profits for the year are likely to be between 381 and 395 million stg, up from 373 million previously, with a total dividend payout of 36.0-37.6 pence per share compared with 28.53 pence.
For the regulated water and sewerage business, the key issue remains the one-off tax on "excess profits" proposed by the new Labour government.
The Labour party, which took power with a huge majority after the May election, has made the so-called "windfall" tax on privatised utilities a key plank of its first budget, scheduled for July 2.
Companies have made representations to the Treasury over the tax and analysts said they would be looking for any indication from Severn Trent on its stance.
Water firms have also been told they will face mandatory leakage targets as part of the government's crack down to handle the country's current severe drought.

At a crisis summit in mid-May, water companies were given three weeks to submit comments on a 10-point plan aimed at tackling the drought and Severn Trent will also be eyed for an update on these proposals.
Outside the core business, Severn Trent's waste operation, Biffa, could provide some added interest.
Biffa saw profits rise 13 percent at the half year and the company is aiming for 15-20 percent growth in profitability at such non-core businesses annually.
But there are concerns that waste management could disappoint, the analyst said.
